newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Telecom year pre-tax profit rises 76 pct.
newsitem.headline: Irish Telecom year pre-tax profit rises 76 pct.

text.p: that pre-tax profit in the year ended April 3, 1997 soared by 76 percent to 204 million punts ($306.9 million), driven by a buoyant Irish economy.
The telecommunications company said turnover increased by 11 percent to a record 1.22 billion punts, despite price cuts of 65 million, with growth in telephone traffic the driving force.
"We are clearly reaping the benefits of a buoyant Irish economy which has created very strong cashflows for the company," chairman Ron Bolger said.
"The financial figures are now coming right and we are on course to ensure we are in a position of financial health to face full competition."
Telecom, in which the state holds a majority stake, said it cut its debt by 330 million punts to 373 million during the year and slashed its debt/equity ratio to 0.45 from 1.4.

A total of 180 million of the debt reduction came from operating activities while 150 million was the result of a cash injection from two new shareholders, PTT Nederland NV and Sweden's Telia, which purchased a 20 percent stake as part of a strategic alliance last year.
On the operational front, Telecom said total traffic grew by 14 percent against 12 percent a year earlier while new line connections grew by five percent to 171,300.
"This is the highest number of connections ever achieved by Telecom Eireann in a single year," the company said.
It said that total lines at year-end were up six percent to 1.39 million while mobile phone growth was exceptionally strong, with the customer base increasing by 83 percent to 288,600.
Bolger said the challenge for the future was to continue a strategy of business growth and cost reduction while maintaining an aggressive price reduction strategy and investing for the future.
Since 1995 Telecom has announced price cuts worth 210 million punts.

"Important though the progress on reducing prices has been, we are still far from a position where our overall level of charges could be sustained in the fully competitive marketplace in the year 2000," chief executive Alfie Kane said. "So the continued downward spiral of prices is set to continue into the future."
Telecom has also cut costs, reducing its operating costs to turnover ratio to 54 percent from 58 percent over the last two years.
"Our dedication to cost reduction remains undiminished: it is one of the keys to the survival of the company in the open marketplace," Kane said. ($ = 0.664 Irish Pounds)
